title: Object-ball throw versus cut angle and shot speed
purpose: Validates the 1/7 sticking constant, the Coulomb cap on the tangential impulse and the speed-dependent friction coefficient. Also records a known model limitation (see known_deviations).
sources: Alciatore, 'The Amazing World of Billiards Physics' (2007), TP A-14 throw data

params.note: object ball placed along the cut-angle bisector per row; the cue ball is spinless, so the slip is purely horizontal

known_deviations: The friction between the balls falls with the sliding speed (TP A.14's fit to Marlow's data, doc section 4.4.5), so the throw falls with the shot speed: the model gives 4.81 deg at a 30 deg cut on TP A.14's slow shot (1 mph) and 2.02 deg on its fast one (7 mph). The measured values are 4.65 and 2.90 deg. The slow end is close and the fast end is under-predicted by about 0.9 deg.
In the sticking regime (cut angles below ~18.8 deg) the model predicts atan(2*tan(cut)/(7*(1+e))), which gives 1.48 deg at a 10 deg cut against a measured 1.45 deg - agreement to 0.03 deg.

The measured throw depends on the cue ball's spin as well as its speed, and the published figures do not carry every shot condition, so the residual is a calibration item rather than a structural one (doc section 14.3).
